text: The package code rwb-integration is assigned is named by no source, so the story is built and tested on the legacy ALLOCATION fixtures as synthetic test data: package ALLOCATION, versions ALLOC-2026.11, ALLOC-2026.12, ALLOC-2026.13 and TRF-2026.11, rows ALLOC-014, ALLOC-015, ALLOC-031, ALLOC-032, ALLOC-040, ALLOC-041 and ALLOC-999, scenarios TA-07 and TA-19, queues MTG-BKK-CO, MTG-UPC-CO, MTG-CEN-CO and GEN-CO, 24 and 26 rows, 50 scenarios, checksum 9f2c...e1b4 and valid from 2026-12-15. The assigned code, its version labels and its target queues are read at run time through the rwb-case reference-data contract and never appear in code.
why: Every DP-04 consuming story needs a package to load and evaluate, and neither the plan, the Ownership Map, the two design decks nor the legacy story names the package of rwb-integration; the legacy ALLOCATION values are the only ones the sources give, and inventing a code would be worse than reusing them as fixtures.
read: WP B-P2-03 story line; legacy RWB-E1-073 sections 7, 9 and 16; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 15 and 27; Recovery Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 15 and 16; RWB-ITG-E1073-ITG section 10 and its AC of the same shape.
confirm: Reference-data owner of rwb-case (RWB-P3-E1043-CON) and the rwb-decision registry owner, before SIT
impact: A different assigned package changes fixtures and reference rows only; no behaviour, no code and no contract changes.

text: The model fetch is fixed for this run as GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/rule-models/{packageCode}/{versionLabel}, answering the model with its generated DRL, its state, its valid-from date, its SHA-256 checksum and the scenario set stored with the version, with 404 for an unknown label and 503 for an unavailable registry; the path segments, the request fields and the response fields are agreed with the rwb-decision owner at the contract review.
why: Architecture v5 slides 14 and 27 name only GET /rule-models/{n}/{v} and neither the Ownership Map nor API Specification v4 carries the operation, so a story cannot be built or contract-tested without a default; the placeholder alone would leave the client, the checksum check and the four fakes unspecified.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14, 27 and 41; Ownership Map v1 API rows (no rule-models operation); RWB-P6-E1073-APP section 12.2 and 12.8 (the same sibling shape); Template and Rules v1 section R4 (base /api/recovery/<short>/v1).
confirm: Contract owner of RWB-P7-E1073-CON at the contract review, with the rwb-decision registry owner
impact: A renamed path or field touches one client, one fake and one section of this story; no business value changes.

text: The plan's dependency rows are followed as written: Depends on (build) is None, the contract dependency is RWB-P3-E1073-CON and there is no I or X row. The eight H rows the DP table adds (RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-E1072-CON, RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, RWB-PLT-E1071-CON, RWB-PLT-E1047-CON, RWB-PLT-E1044-CON, RWB-PLT-N001-CON) are read as wave-0 platform prerequisites of the service template, the Drools kit and the workflow kit included, so the lane L-P2-D and the Day-1 start do not change; the DP-04 C row RWB-P7-E1073-CON is the contract faked for the model fetch alongside the plan's RWB-P3-E1073-CON.
why: The plan and the DP table disagree on both the H rows and the C row, and a story cannot carry two dependency lists; the R-PREC order and the sibling slices of this same legacy key follow the plan's list, and treating the platform contracts as wave-0 prerequisites keeps the Day-1 rule of section R5.7 intact.
read: WP B-P2-03 story line; Template and Rules v1 sections R5.4, R5.5 (DP-03, DP-04, DP-06, DP-07, DP-10, DP-14, DP-15, DP-19) and R5.7; Ownership Map v1 (rule_package, rule_package_version, rule_row and rule_test_case to P7 under ASM-A6-tables-3); RWB-P6-E1073-APP section 13.
confirm: Solution architect at the Service Contract Catalog review, with the platform and rwb-decision owners
impact: If the H rows become real build dependencies the lane waits for the wave-0 contract stories; the behaviour of the local load does not change.

text: The local copy lives in one table of rwb_integration created by migration V1073_1__local_rule_copy.sql, with a unique key on (package_code, version_label) and an index on the state, and holds the package code, version label, SHA-256 checksum, state, valid from, loaded at and the local run record of a refusal; the table name, the column names and the types are fixed by the rwb_integration DB story and are carried as "local model copy" until then.
why: No source names the local copy table or its columns, and DP-01 and DP-15 require the copy to be a table of this service's own schema written by its own Flyway sequence; leaving it unnamed would break the migration, the repository and the LRU restart behaviour of AC1 and AC5.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-073 section 13 (no new table; the registry tables are RWB-E1-072's); Architecture v5 slide 20 (own schema with decision_record) and slide 27 (each service holds its own approved copy); Template and Rules v1 sections R5.5 DP-01 and DP-15; Ownership Map v1 (outbox_event, processed_event and idempotency_key to PLT under ASM-A6-tables-8).
confirm: ACE DB owner and the rwb_integration DB story, before the rwb_integration baseline is created
impact: A different table or column set touches one migration, one repository and one section of this story; the behaviour is unchanged.

text: Architecture v5 slide 20 governs who consumes RulePackageInForce: every service refreshes its cache on it, so rwb-integration is an evaluator, despite slide 43 row 30 listing only rwb-case, rwb-valuation, rwb-treatment and rwb-payment. The event carries the package code, the version label, the SHA-256 checksum and the valid-from date and nothing else, and is consumed with inbox dedupe, retry 1 min, 10 min, 1 h then .dlt.
why: Two slides of the same catalogue disagree on the consumer list, and the payload is not published anywhere; a story cannot consume an event whose shape is open, and the sibling slices of this legacy key read slide 20.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 20 (every service: RulePackageInForce to cache refresh) and slide 43 row 30 (four named consumers); Recovery Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 11 and 15 (each owning service loads a version on RulePackageInForce); RWB-ITG-E1073-ITG section 12.4.
confirm: Solution architect and the rwb-decision event owner at the architecture review, before wave 1 build
impact: If the payload gains a field the consumer ignores it until the contract changes; if the consumer list were read instead, this service would have no rule copy and no local evaluation.

text: rules.testcases.min = 50 and drools.kiebase.cache.max = 20 are read on the business date through the parameters contract of rwb-case, under the legacy parameter codes of RWB-E1-042; the read path and the row identifiers of parameter_catalog and parameter_value are agreed with the rwb-case owner, and neither value is a constant, a values-file entry or a default in code.
why: DP-06 moves parameters to rwb-case and the plan sets no parameter dependency for this story; no source gives the target read path or the row identifiers, and the values themselves must not be written in code under BR12.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-073 sections 3 and 13 (rules.testcases.min = 50 assumed, drools.kiebase.cache.max = 20); Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-06 and section R3 default ruling; Ownership Map v1 (parameter_catalog and parameter_value to P3); RWB-P6-E1073-APP section 12.2.
confirm: Parameter owner of rwb-case (RWB-P3-E1042-CON) before the contract review
impact: A changed value or row is data and needs no release; the story behaviour is unaffected.

text: MSG-P3-027 keeps the legacy text "The rule version was refused at the {check} check: {detail}.", and the local load adds two {check} values to the six the legacy story fixes: checksum and package state, with {detail} naming the package, the two checksums, the state, the row, cell or scenario IDs and never a file payload or a personal value.
why: The legacy message enumerates compile, schema, overlap, unreachable row, default row and scenario and stops there, while this slice refuses a load on the checksum and on the registry state before any of those run; no source gives the wording of the two added values or of the message prefix.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-073 section 14 (MSG-P3-027 and its {check} values); RWB-P6-E1073-APP section 14; Error and Message Standard (prefix family); Architecture v5 slide 27 (verify checksum before swap).
confirm: Error and Message Standard owner, before the message catalogue is frozen
impact: One alert and one log text change; no behaviour changes.

text: The scenario set of a version travels in the model-fetch answer with the model: at least rules.testcases.min (50) cases, each with its facts, its expected queue or outcome and its scenario ID, so the local runner re-runs exactly the set that gated the version at rwb-decision. No second operation is added for it.
why: The design says the version's scenarios gate the load at rwb-decision and are stored with the version, while this slice must re-run them locally before the swap; no source says how they reach the service, and a second endpoint would add a contract this run cannot publish.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-073 sections 4 and 13 (Rules tab, RuleScenarioRunner, rules.testcases.min); Recovery Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 15 (50+ scenarios per version, checksum and DRL stored with it); Architecture v5 slide 27 (verify, swap, keep the last good model); RWB-ITG-E1073-ITG section 12.4.
confirm: Contract owner of RWB-P7-E1073-CON at the contract review
impact: If the scenarios travel separately, the loader makes one more read with the same check; the refusal behaviour is unchanged.

text: The rwb-integration service runs as one login created with the rwb_integration schema by the platform DB work (DP-02); the story names it "the rwb-integration login" until the name is agreed and carries it as a secret reference in the chart.
why: No source gives the login name and every DP-02 row requires one login per service; the legacy story ran on the shared recovery_svc login, which the target retires.
read: WP B-P2-03 story line; Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-02; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 29 and 41 (one schema and one login per service); RWB-P2-E2001-APP section 3 (the same sibling default).
confirm: ACE DB owner and the platform DB story, before the rwb_integration baseline is created
impact: None on behaviour: the login is named by role and swapped for the agreed name without a content change.

text: The TSD P2 Integration v3 wording that IntegrationService "writes the decision log entry before any change" is read as the DP-03 one-transaction rule: the local decision record, the state change and the outbox row are written in one transaction in rwb_integration, and a failed record write leaves the change uncommitted instead of being written ahead of it.
why: The monolith wrote the log entry first because the log and the change sat behind separate calls; under DP-03 and R-UNI-39 the record and the change are one local transaction, and a separate write ahead of the change would leave a record of a change that never happened.
read: TSD P2 Integration v3 T2 (IntegrationService); FSD P2 Integration v3 A2.1 to A2.7 step 3; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 28 (saved with the change, one transaction; strict mode); Recovery Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 14 (RecordAndApply, one transaction); Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-03.
confirm: Risk and Internal Audit at the ADR-009 and ADR-022 review, with the rwb-decision ledger owner
impact: A record written ahead of the change would need a compensating rule and a gap alert; the one-transaction reading keeps the legacy guarantee that nothing moves without a record.

text: The rwb-integration service runs as one login created with the rwb_integration schema by the platform DB work (DP-02); this story names it "the rwb-integration login" until the name is agreed and carries it as a secret reference in the chart.
why: No source gives the login name and every DP-02 row requires one login per service; the legacy story ran on the shared recovery_svc identity.
read: RWB-P2-E4046-APP sections 3, 10 and 13; DP-02 in Template and Rules section R5.5; Architecture v5 slide 41 (one schema and one login per service); RWB-P2-E1007-APP section 3.
confirm: ACE DB owner and the platform DB story, before the rwb_integration baseline is created
impact: None on behaviour: the login is named by role and swapped for the agreed name without a content change.

text: The ALS settlement booking is modelled as one outbound item on an interface configuration row of rwb-integration, as the legacy key RWB-E4-046 and RWB-ITG-E4046-ITG state it; the FSD P2 Integration v3 A1.5 register and the TSD P2 Integration v3 T1 and T5.1 line that give INT-03 core-bank bookings no Workbench interface are read as superseded for this legacy key, and the booked position is still read back from the ACE data by rwb-source-data after the next ACE batch.
why: Two sources disagree and a story has to be built on one reading. The FSD and the TSD describe the booking as manual and confirmed through v_ace_account; the legacy story, the integration story and the Ownership Map put the outbound item and its lifecycle in rwb-integration. Taking the FSD line would leave the legacy key with no outbound interface at all and would contradict the integration story this slice is bound by.
read: FSD P2 Integration v3 A1.5; TSD P2 Integration v3 T1 and T5.1; legacy RWB-E4-046 sections Story and AC1; RWB-ITG-E4046-ITG steps 4, 5, 10 and section 19; Architecture v5 slide 41 (rwb-integration owns interface config and outbound items); Ownership Map v1 rows for interface_config and outbound_item.
confirm: Solution architect at the Service Contract Catalog review, with the P2, P8, P1 and S2 owners, before the wave 3 entry check
impact: If the FSD reading were kept, this story would shrink to nothing and the legacy key would lose its outbound interface; the read-back half and the case and ledger halves do not change either way.

text: The ALS interface id, its transport, its message or file layout and file pattern, the control totals of the layout, the maximum attempts, the retry intervals, the owner role and the alert role are values of one versioned interface_config row loaded per environment through the reference-data load; the story and its criteria assert "the version in force" and name no value, and an absent or not-yet-valid row is refused with MSG-GEN-001 naming the field and writes no item.
why: No source gives any of these values for the ALS booking. The FSD register names four interfaces only and the retry values it shows belong to the WIN file example. A story cannot be built or contract-tested without a default, and naming a value would be inventing a business value.
read: FSD P2 Integration v3 A1.5 and A2.1.4.3; TSD P2 Integration v3 T3.1 (interface_config DF-OPS-136 to DF-OPS-148) and T4; RWB-ITG-E4046-ITG section 3 ('The ALS interface ID, its transport, the message or file layout and the test endpoint are not specified'); Template and Rules section R9 (placeholder).
confirm: Interface owner of the ALS booking and the reference-data administrator, at the contract review of RWB-P2-E1007-CON
impact: The values arrive as one row per environment and are changed without a release; if the interface turns out not to be a file, the transport component changes and the item lifecycle does not.

text: Each state change of the item that matters writes one local decision record in rwb_integration in the same local transaction as the change: the creation of the item, its move to EXCEPTION and its resend. The record carries the interface id, the item id, the business date, the attempt count and the outcome, and the library publishes DecisionRecorded on rwb.decision-record.v1; the record takes the default decision code of the library until the rule registry publishes one for the outbound path, and the treatment record and the central ledger entry stay with rwb-treatment and rwb-decision.
why: DP-03 writes the record locally in the owning service in the same transaction as that service's own change, and this is the service whose change is the sending of the booking. The legacy story declares no decision of its own ('Decision: None') and no source says which of the three outbound state changes carries a record or which code it takes.
read: Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 18 and slide 26 (local record with the state change, central ledger, point of no return) and slide 14 (record fields); Template and Rules section R5.5 DP-03; Architecture v5 slide 20 (own schema with decision_record) and slide 43 (DecisionRecorded); legacy RWB-E4-046 metadata row Decision.
confirm: Risk and Internal Audit at the ADR-022 review, with the rwb-decision ledger owner
impact: If only the exception and the resend need a record, the creation drops one write and the blocking rule of AC6 is unchanged.

text: The ten fields of outbound_item (DF-OPS-168 to DF-OPS-177) and the thirteen fields of interface_config (DF-OPS-136 to DF-OPS-148) as published in TSD P2 Integration v3 T3.1 carry the slice; no column is added to either table, the treatment id and the document id ride in case_ids and payload_ref, and the mapping of each element of the ALS message or file to a field is left to the layout of the interface row.
why: The TSD publishes the field sets but not the mapping of the ALS layout to them, and no source gives a column this story would need beyond the ten and the thirteen. Adding a column would break DP-15 and the boundary rule for no proven need.
read: TSD P2 Integration v3 T3.1 (interface_config and outbound_item field sets) and T3.3 (relationships); legacy RWB-E4-046 data table (outbound_item DF-OPS-168 to DF-OPS-177); RWB-ITG-E4046-ITG section 11 ('Which of the ten outbound_item field IDs carries each field the harness reads ... are not specified'); Architecture v5 slide 41.
confirm: Solution architect and the data model owner, before the rwb_integration migration sequence is frozen
impact: A field the ALS layout needs beyond the ten is a column added by one migration of the service's own sequence and touches no other schema.

text: The one task the exception queue raises is created through the rwb-case contract with the case ids of the item, the owner role of the interface row and the item and treatment named in its text; its task code is agreed with the rwb-case owner at the contract review and no code is assumed here.
why: The FSD and the TSD say a task goes to owner_role and name no task code for an outbound item; the legacy build notes raise a task for the role in owner_role and name a code only for the outbox delivery path, which is not this one.
read: FSD P2 Integration v3 AC-EXC-P2-001-01 ('a task for role RW-PLATADM'); TSD P2 Integration v3 T4 ('a task goes to owner_role') and T-A; legacy RWB-E4-046 permission checks; RWB-P2-E1007-APP section 4 step 9 and section 12.2 (the task raised through the rwb-case action).
confirm: rwb-case contract owner, at the contract review of the P3 action operation
impact: A different task code touches one call and its fake; the item state and the exception queue do not change.

text: A positive acknowledgement result sets the item ACKNOWLEDGED and publishes FileDelivered; a negative result or a timeout counts as a failed attempt and follows the retry path, and only a result the row's own code list marks non-retryable skips the retries and moves the item to EXCEPTION at once. The result codes are a list of the interface row, not an enumeration in code.
why: No source gives the ALS acknowledgement codes or says how a rejection maps to the retry ladder. R-RES-23 requires a rejection to become visible on the officer queue and the FSD requires the retry and exception behaviour for a failed send, so a mapping is needed and a non-retryable list is the only reading that keeps both.
read: FSD P2 Integration v3 A2.2, A2.3 and AC-EXC-P2-001-01; TSD P2 Integration v3 T4 and T5.1 ('acknowledgement by the receiver'); Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-RES-22 and R-RES-23; RWB-ITG-E4046-ITG steps 10 and 11.
confirm: Interface owner of the ALS booking, with the operations booking team, before wave 3 build
impact: If every rejection must be retried in full, the non-retryable list is empty and one branch of the mapper is dropped; the exception queue and the task are unchanged.

text: The metadata H row of the story stays None as the plan fixes it, while DP-03 and DP-19 add H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON and H RWB-PLT-N001-CON: both are platform contract stories delivered by the platform wave, the story builds against them and their fakes from Day 1, and neither blocks the start. The legacy key names no feature switch, so the slice runs behind the platform flag library's key for the outbound path, whose value is not named here.
why: The plan writes the H row as None and the DP table adds two platform contracts, so the two statements have to be reconciled without changing the plan's row. The flag key is named by no source, and inventing one would put a business value in a story.
read: WP B-P2-03 story line for RWB-P2-E4046-APP ("H": []); Template and Rules section R5.5 DP-03 and DP-19 and section R5.7 (H points only to the same service or a platform CON story); Architecture v5 slide 20 (every service from the service template and shared libraries); legacy RWB-E4-046 (no feature flag row).
confirm: Solution architect at the wave 3 entry check
impact: None on behaviour: the platform wave delivers both contracts before wave 3 and the flag only gates the path.

text: One outbound item exists per interface and Idempotency-Key. The key is minted by the caller, this service neither rewrites nor derives it, a repeat of the same key returns the existing item and creates no second row, file or event, and the pair is enforced by a unique index on outbound_item (interface_id, idempotency_key) added by one migration of the rwb-integration sequence where the base does not already carry it.
why: Architecture v5 slide 11 requires an Idempotency-Key on every POST and a unique file id, and the FSD resend case needs one item per key to be meaningful; no source gives the key format or the constraint that enforces the pair for this table.
read: Architecture v5 slide 11 (Idempotency-Key on every POST; fileId unique; re-delivery safe); TSD P2 Integration v3 T3.1 (outbound_item.idempotency_key, required) and T3.0; FSD P2 Integration v3 AC-EXC-P2-001-04; legacy RWB-E4-046 guardrails; RWB-ITG-E4046-ITG step 4 (one item for the treatment and one Idempotency-Key).
confirm: Contract owner of RWB-P2-E1007-CON, before the activity contract is frozen
impact: A caller that mints a new key per attempt would create several items for one treatment; the caller's workflow id is what prevents that and is stated in the story.
